sentences.text: The meeting, identified as the second session, discussed conceptual design properties, materials, user interface, and trends for a new TV remote control.
The team evaluated a prototype against specific criteria, including 'fancy look and feel' and 'technological innovation', and reached a consensus on several design features.
Participants agreed on a kinetic battery, a clamshell structure with a plastic body and rubberized cover, and an LCD screen on the top half with rubber buttons on the bottom.
Participant A noted that the previous meeting decided on a universal control handset for all TV video equipment that must be accessible to a wide range of consumers and ages.

Participant A acknowledged a potential dissonance between the desired product image (uncluttered, undaunting) and the actual budget, and noted that consumers consider teletext outdated with the internet.
Participant D explained that most existing remote controls are chunky because they must fit triple A batteries and have a wireless range of up to about five metres.
Participant D reported that 75% of users find most remote controls ugly, 80% would spend more money if a remote control looked fancy, and 50% of users only use 10% of the buttons.
Participant B reported that 50% of users are frustrated that remote controls are often lost or slip down the back of the sofa, and 34% take too much time to learn to use the remote control.
Participant B reported that slightly more than a quarter of people said repetitive strain injury (shoulder and elbow problems) is bad due to small movements of the remote control.

Participant B reported that the vast majority of the 35 and under age group would like a liquid crystal display (LCD) and speech recognition features, while this preference reverses in the 35 to 45 and older age groups.
Participant A suggested using a pack on the TV to hide the remote so users cannot see it, allowing them to press a button on top of the TV that beeps to indicate its location.
Participant A proposed that the corporate logo be incorporated into the handset design to make it fashionable and trendy, noting that people pay more for devices that look good.
Participant B noted that attractive features will differ between a trendy New Yorker and a retired South African, implying a need for varied designs across international markets.
The team decided to leave out voice recognition.
The team decided on a flip design.
The team decided on a different shape from the normal shell design.
The team decided to use infrared transmission for the remote control, placing the sender on the front of the bottom layer.
The team decided to incorporate a company logo on the inside of the product, either as a bezzled logo, an inset, or an engraving, ensuring it does not interfere with the outside.
Participants A, B, and C agreed on the use of a kinetic battery.
Participant B stated that the group decided on a rubber casing for the plastic shell with a variety of designs.
Participant B stated that the group will use vegetable and fruit colours for the rubber cover but will not attempt to make the shell itself look like a vegetable or fruit.
Participant C stated the group will incorporate the company logo into the design.

Participant B confirmed that the group discussed a beeper for location tracking at the last meeting, and Participant A stated that the group is looking into a beeper for location tracking via a company memo.
Participant B proposed using a seven-point scale (1 = true, 7 = false) to evaluate the prototype against criteria, with the option to collect individual ratings and calculate an average.
Participant B mentioned that the team is waiting for Participant F's rating to complete the calculation for the 'technologically innovative' criterion.
